_comment: Config for the weekly sharded mutation run.
SCOPE: RUNNERCORE + CORE + WORKER -- the whole logic tier. ~15,900 LOC,
~2,650 mutants, 12 shards of ~70 minutes. Widened to Core after run 3 came
back green (84%), and to Worker after the 2026-08-25 sweep emptied the
survivor queue (366 killed, 6 survived, all six answered) -- each widening
one target at a time, after a green run, per the original plan.
SHARD COUNT IS SET BY FIXED COST, NOT BY MUTANTS. Measured across run 3's
shards: ~29 minutes of fixed overhead each (a cold build of the project
inside Muter's copy, plus the unmutated baseline run), then a per-mutant
cost of the suite run -- ~9.8s under the old skip, ~11-12s with the full
suite (probe run 32916211705). Twelve shards puts ~220 mutants on each:
~40 min of mutants over ~29 min of fixed cost, the same wall-clock the
8-shard RunnerCore+Core sweep had.
WORKER'S ADMISSION WAS MEASURED, NOT DECLARED, and the two probe runs that
did it are worth knowing about because each killed a standing belief:
* Run 32913719441 ran the full suite (WorkerTests included) unprivileged,
20 times: 20/20 FAILED, identically, on
sandboxedRunnerTimeoutReapsBackgroundChildProcess -- 'unshare: Operation
not permitted'. The sandbox's namespace primitive needs --privileged on
the container, exactly as the worker-tests CI job already sets. So the
weekly workflow's mutate job and mutation-pr's job both carry
--privileged; without it every Worker-era baseline is deterministically
red before a single mutant runs. NOT a flake -- a capability.
* Run 32916211705 ran the same thing privileged: 20/20 PASSED at 11-12s
per iteration, dead flat, on a 4-core hosted runner. The 48
'timing-sensitive' WorkerTests the sweep used to skip survived every
round -- the one genuine flake this class ever produced (the
daemon-fanout 100ms overlap race, 2026-08-25 shard 1) had already been
fixed by making the overlap a rendezvous. The old caveat that the suite
'must first be made survivable in this configuration' is resolved by
measurement, not waived.
So --skip WorkerTests/ is GONE from testArgs: Sources/Worker mutants are
graded by the tests that cover them, and the 48 re-admitted tests also
grade RunnerCore and Core mutants. The watch-item for the first widened
runs: a mutant that breaks timeout logic can hold its suite run toward
mutationTestTimeout (900s in mutation-run.sh) -- if Worker shards run long,
look there first.
CORE SURVIVORS CARRY A CAVEAT THAT RUNNERCORE'S AND WORKER'S DO NOT. The
suite skips APITests -- unavoidably, since it dominates the runtime -- and
Core is exercised through it. Measured by static reference: 89% of Core's
LOC is reachable from CoreTests or WorkerTests, 5% only from APITests, and
6% from no test at all. So a Core survivor in one of those APITests-only
files may be an artefact of the skip rather than a hole, exactly as a
missing interpreter would be -- all four achievement-family survivors of the
2026-08-25 sweep were this shape. Check such a survivor against the full
suite before writing a test for it, and put the test in the layer that owns
the invariant (docs/mutation-triage.md).
--skip ZipProcessEnvironmentTests IS LOAD-BEARING. Muter writes
`import class Foundation.ProcessInfo` into every file it mutates before the
baseline runs, and that suite scans two Sources/Core files for `Process(`
constructions -- so with Core in scope the preamble reaches the files it
reads. The general rule: a test asserting on the TEXT of a file
under mutation cannot coexist with mutation, and has no mutants worth
killing anyway.
-Xswiftc -no-warnings-as-errors IS LOAD-BEARING. The package builds with
.treatAllWarnings(as: .error), and RemoveSideEffects deletes the USE of a
binding, leaving `let x = ...` unused -- a warning, therefore an error,
therefore a copy that does not compile and a shard that yields zero mutants.
APIServer is excluded permanently, not pending: 94k LOC, ~15,700 mutants that
must be graded by APITests, ~1,712h serial -- ~96% of the tree's cost for its
least informative mutants. Triage scales with SURVIVORS, and a report nobody
can read is worse than none because it looks like coverage.
